newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater figure pleads innocent to state charges.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater figure pleads innocent to state charges.

text.p: The government witness who implicated President Clinton in the Whitewater scandal, former Arkansas business executive David Hale, pleaded innocent Friday to state charges.

The Whitewater special prosecutor, Kenneth W. Starr, had attempted to persuade an Arkansas prosecutor to postpone or even drop his case against Hale, who was accompanied in court by the deputy Whitewater special prosector, Ray Jahn.
Jahn denied attempting to pressure Arkansas authorities.

"We recognise that the district attorney represents the sovereign state of Arkansas, and Mr. Hale needs to put his faith in the jurors of Arkansas, just as we put our faith in the jurors of Arkansas in the first Whitewater trial," Jahn said.
Hale is accused of looting a state-chartered burial insurance company he owned. The company is in default.

In the first jury trial of the Whitewater investigation, Hale testified that Clinton had pressured him to make an illegal $300,000 loan to Susan McDougal, who was a partner of President and Mrs. Clinton in a failed Arkansas real estate project in the 1970s.
Clinton testified by videotape for the defence and denied Hale's allegation. But the jury convicted McDougal, her former husband and Arkansas Gov. Jim Guy Tucker of fraud and conspiracy.
Hale is presently serving a 23-month sentence for defrauding the Small Business Administration through a loan company he operated.
